result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-028.md: the real check-in implementation on top of REQ-018's authorization-only /checkin stub -- manual (no QR) door check-in list, live counter, search, and the S6 write-time recheck that makes AC1's stale-toggle refusal genuine.

SCHEMA CHECK (Sec0, mandatory pre-check) -- NO CHANGE NEEDED, confirmed by direct inspection of db/schema.ts: checked_in_by (uuid, references users.id, line 257) and check_in_method (native pgEnum 'check_in_method' ['qr','manual'], line 260) BOTH ALREADY EXIST -- only checked_in_at was confirmed at REQ-011/022, but the other two were added in the same original REQ-011 schema pass and were simply never used by any handler until now. Additionally found a pre-existing DB-level CHECK constraint (chk_registrations_checked_in_only_if_admitted, sql: checked_in_at IS NULL OR admission = 'admitted', schema.ts lines 295-298) added under REQ-011 specifically for S6 -- this design's application-level write-time recheck (Sec3) is a second, cooperating enforcement layer on top of that constraint, not a replacement for it. DATA-DESIGNER does NOT run this cycle.

TELEGRAM SEARCH-BOX INTERACTION DECIDED (Sec1): explicitly REJECTED the task's suggested 'render list, then interpret the next free-text message as a search query' pattern, for a structural reason specific to this codebase -- no session/conversation-state mechanism exists anywhere in apps/bot/src (grep confirmed), and the two ways to add one are both worse than the alternative: in-memory state is exactly the negative case security-invariants.md S9 already names as unacceptable ('idempotency enforced by an in-memory set a restart clears'), and a DB-backed pending-search column is a genuine schema change with an unspecified expiry policy that no AC asks for. DECIDED INSTEAD: '/checkin <event_id> [query text]' -- the search query is an OPTIONAL SECOND ARGUMENT consuming the remainder of the command text (not a single token, since names contain spaces), stateless, restart-safe, matching this codebase's own established 'command plus free-text remainder' convention (matchText). Flagged as Open Question 3 (Sec6) that this is less discoverable than a persistent search box -- mitigated only by a footer hint string (checkin.searchHint), not fully resolved.

PAGINATION / callback_data BUDGET WORKED OUT EXPLICITLY (Sec1.4-1.5): Telegram's 64-byte callback_data cap means 'checkin:toggle:<registrationId>' (51 bytes, one UUID) cannot ALSO carry eventId (a second UUID) -- so the toggle callback carries ONLY registrationId, and the toggle handler recovers eventId from its own fresh read inside toggleCheckIn (Sec3.2 step 6) rather than from callback_data. This is also what makes the toggle structurally incapable of carrying a stale admission snapshot -- there is nothing in the button for a snapshot to live in. Full (unfiltered) list is paginated (PAGE_SIZE=10, callback_data carries eventId+pageNumber, fits easily); search results are NOT paginated -- capped at SEARCH_RESULT_LIMIT=20 with a truncation note, sidestepping the budget question for that view entirely, since the query text is never encoded into any callback_data. After a toggle, the handler edits the EXISTING message's keyboard in place (replacing only the one matching button) rather than re-rendering from scratch, so whatever page/search view the staff member was on is preserved without needing to thread it through callback_data at all.

S6 WRITE-TIME RECHECK (Sec3, the crux of AC1) -- decideCheckinToggleOutcome (pure, first-match-wins table: not-found / refused-not-admitted / check-in / undo) plus toggleCheckIn (transactional: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE fresh read of admission/checked_in_at INSIDE the transaction, decide, then conditionally UPDATE + exactly one writeAuditLog call in the same transaction), mirroring withdrawRegistration/reconfirmRegistration's already-established row-lock-then-decide-then-write shape in domain/registration.ts exactly. AC1's negative case is defended structurally, not by convention: the callback_data that triggers this call carries only registrationId (per the budget finding above), so there is no stale value anywhere in the call chain for the decision to trust -- the FOR UPDATE SELECT is the ONLY source of admission this function ever reads. Undo (Sec3.2 step 5) clears ONLY checked_in_at, per the requirement's literal wording -- checked_in_by/check_in_method are left stale (harmless: unconditionally overwritten by the next check-in) rather than also being cleared, since no AC or requirement line asks for that.

RE-AUTHORIZATION AT WRITE TIME (Sec3.3, S2 defense in depth): requireEventStaffForEvent (REQ-018, reused byte-for-byte unchanged) is called again by BOTH the toggle callback and the page-turn callback, not only by the original /checkin command -- a staff member removed mid-shift (/staff_remove) is refused on their very next tap, not only their next /checkin invocation. Flagged as Open Question 4 (Sec6) that this adds one authorization round-trip per page tap, a deliberate S2 choice not an oversight.

PHONE/EMAIL EXCLUSION (AC3, S3): listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin's SELECT clause (Sec2.1) structurally never names profiles.phone/profiles.email -- nothing to filter out post-fetch because it is never fetched. displayName fallback rule (a table, not code) falls back to '@tgUsername' then a fixed placeholder string when both firstName/lastName are absent -- tgUsername is used because S3 names phone/email specifically, not username.

LIVE COUNTER (AC4, Sec2.2): countCheckedIn -- one SELECT count(*) WHERE checked_in_at IS NOT NULL, re-run fresh on every render path (initial list, every page turn, every search, every post-toggle header re-render) with no cache/column/in-memory counter anywhere; nothing in this design writes to the events table. Admission is deliberately NOT added as a second filter predicate since the pre-existing CHECK constraint (Sec0) already makes checked_in_at IS NOT NULL and admission='admitted' equivalent in the live table -- stated explicitly so it doesn't read as a missed filter.

All 6 ACs mapped to concrete design elements in Sec8's table. 4 open questions stated explicitly in Sec6: a stale toggled-away row's button label is not self-correcting until the next full render (deliberate, no AC requires it); the no-op page-indicator button pattern is new to this codebase (no existing precedent); the search pattern's discoverability; and the added authorization round-trip per page turn. No new design-system token/component (Sec7) -- Telegram inline buttons render plain text only, so the checked-in glyph is a plain Unicode character chosen at copy time, not a Lucide icon.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 1b) -- DATA-DESIGNER does not run this cycle, no stored-data change (checked_in_by, check_in_method, and the S6 CHECK constraint all already exist from REQ-011's original schema pass; only checked_in_at had been confirmed in use before this requirement).
